- builder: Mid-tier implementer for well-scoped changes with a clear spec: apply a planned edit, write a test from a described behavior, mechanical refactors, doc/report updates. Give it exact files and acceptance criteria. Not for open-ended design or ambiguous debugging - keep those in the orchestrator session.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- nori-change-documenter: Creates documentation about changes to a codebase. Call the nori-change-documenter whenever you change the codebase. Provide all of the relevance context for *why* the change was made. Be extremely detailed! Provide as much context as possible so the agent can accurately update documentation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-codebase-analyzer: Analyzes codebase implementation details. Call the nori-codebase-analyzer agent when you need to find detailed information about specific components. As always, the more detailed your request prompt, the better! :) (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-locator: Locates files, directories, and components relevant to a feature or task. Call `nori-codebase-locator` with human language prompt describing what you're looking for. Basically a "Super Grep/Glob/LS tool" — Use it if you find yourself desiring to use one of these tools more than once. (Tools: Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-pattern-finder: nori-codebase-pattern-finder is a useful subagent_type for finding similar implementations, usage examples, or existing patterns that can be modeled after. It will give you concrete code examples based on what you're looking for! It's sorta like nori-codebase-locator, but it will not only tell you the location of files, it will also give you code details! (Tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS)

- nori-initial-documenter: Creates documentation about a codebase. This agent creates the initial documentation for the codebase; use this agent when you want to create documentation and no existing documentation is present. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-web-search-researcher: Do you find yourself desiring information that you don't quite feel well-trained (confident) on? Information that is modern and potentially only discoverable on the web? Use the nori-web-search-researcher subagent_type today to find any and all answers to your questions! It will research deeply to figure out and attempt to answer your questions! If you aren't immediately satisfied you can get your money back! (Not really - but you can re-run nori-web-search-researcher with an altered prompt in the event you're not satisfied the first time) (Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- reviewer: High-judgment read-only review. Use to check a diff or design for correctness bugs, edge cases, and simpler alternatives before integrating - especially work produced by builder agents. Returns findings with file:line references and severity; does not fix anything.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- scout: Cheap, fast read-only recon, executed on GPT-5.6 Terra (medium reasoning) via the Codex CLI. Use for searches, file inventories, "where is X defined/used", summarizing a file or directory, running read-only bd/git commands or tests and reporting output verbatim. No editing. Delegate here whenever the task is mechanical lookup rather than judgment. Prefer calling `scripts/codex-agent scout` directly from the orchestrator when you can (same isolation, no relay hop; include the recon rules from this file in the prompt); this agent type is the interface for workflow agentType calls and the fallback when codex is unavailable.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- quota-watch: Monitor Amp Free quota and handoff before exhaustion. Use when user says quota-watch, check quota, or monitor usage.
- initialize-noridocs: Initialize docs.md files throughout the codebase
- nori-create-skillset: Create a new custom skillset by cloning an existing skillset
- nori-switch-skillset: Switch between Nori configuration skillsets (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- session-close: Cold-start-readiness check before ending a work session - runs the 3 judgment prompts plus the mechanical backstop, then the standard close/push.
- setup-beads-sync: Set up a private GitHub Dolt repo for personal beads and configure sync for the current project
- switch-nori-profile: Switch between Nori configuration profiles (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- triage: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. content.content:
name: Update vendorHash for dependabot Go bumps

# Dependabot bumps to go.mod/go.sum invalidate the proxyVendor FOD hash in
# default.nix, which fails the nix-build CI gate. This workflow detects the
# drift, computes the new hash via scripts/update-nix-vendorhash.sh, and
# pushes the update back to the dependabot branch so the gate goes green
# without a maintainer round-trip.
#
# Tracked under beads-bz5.
#
# Why pull_request_target (not pull_request):
#   GitHub gives the GITHUB_TOKEN read-only permissions on `pull_request`
#   workflows triggered by dependabot, regardless of declared `permissions:`.
#   `pull_request_target` runs in the trusted context of the base branch with
#   full token permissions, which is required to push back to the PR branch.
#
# Safety against pull_request_target abuse:
#   - The job only runs when github.actor is dependabot[bot] AND the PR head
#     is on the upstream repo (head.repo.full_name == github.repository).
#     Dependabot never opens PRs from forks, so this combination is not
#     reachable from an external contributor.
#   - We explicitly check out the PR head SHA to operate on dependabot's
#     bumped go.mod/go.sum. Because dependabot is the only allowed actor and
#     never modifies scripts/, the trust boundary is the dependabot bot
#     itself — this is the same trust posture the project already accepts
#     when merging dependabot PRs.
#   - No force-push. Single commit with attribution.
#
# Caveat:
#   GitHub does not retrigger pull_request workflow runs for commits
#   authored by GITHUB_TOKEN. After this workflow pushes, the existing
#   nix-build.yml check on this PR will remain stuck on the pre-fix commit.
#   Maintainers either re-run nix-build manually, or this workflow's own
#   success acts as the green signal that the hash is correct.

on:
  pull_request_target:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'go.mod'
      - 'go.sum'

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: update-vendor-hash-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  update-vendor-hash:
    name: Update default.nix vendorHash
    if: >-
      github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout PR head
        uses: actions/checkout@9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v6
        with:
          # pull_request_target defaults to the base ref. Explicitly check
          # out the PR head so we operate on dependabot's bumped go.mod/sum.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Install Nix
        uses: DeterminateSystems/determinate-nix-action@d96678350ffd6a456235832eb11e1c491589b7bb # v3

      - name: Capture pre-update vendorHash
        id: pre
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          OLD_HASH=$(grep 'vendorHash = ' default.nix | sed 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/')
          echo "old_hash=$OLD_HASH" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Pre-update vendorHash: $OLD_HASH"

      - name: Update vendorHash
        run: ./scripts/update-nix-vendorhash.sh

  # Go modules
  - package-ecosystem: "gomod"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"

Sweep complete. All 10 dependabot PRs are dispositioned, and the structural fix is in flight.

## What I found

- **Main was red**, which hard-blocks all merges: last night's Nightly Full Tests failed on `TestInitCancel_E2E` — a Feb-2026 test, green the previous 7 nights, that timed out waiting for a prompt under full-suite load. Classic flake; I reran the failed job (was still running at close).
- **The real problem is structural, not the PRs.** Every Go-module bump rewrites `go.sum`, which invalidates the nix `vendorHash`; the auto-fix workflow pushes a bot commit, after which dependabot refuses to rebase and CI never runs on the new head. That's why #4702 has been stuck since July 10 through ~60 patrol attempts, and why the four fresh gomod PRs (#5017/#5018/#5020/#5021) showed "no checks". Merging them one-by-one would mean an `@dependabot recreate` + full-CI round per merge.

## What I did

- **Opened gastownhall/beads#5038**: adds dependabot `groups` config — gomod minor/patch bumps arrive as **one grouped PR** (majors stay solo so a breaking bump can't block the group), actions and Python deps grouped wholesale. A grouped PR is dependabot-authored, so it gets a single bot-computed vendorHash, and dependabot auto-closes the five superseded gomod singles when it regroups. I rejected hand-rolling a combined PR: no nix on this machine to compute the hash, and the hash workflow only fires for dependabot.
- **Handed the five independent PRs to the patrol** (actions bumps #5015/#5016/#5019, Python dev-deps #5022/#5023 — three fully green, two with one flaky proxied-dolt shard the patrol will rerun), plus #5038 itself. Per repo policy, no in-session merging.
- **Paper trail**: disposition comment on #4702; follow-up bead mybd-ysu1 (blocked on #5038's bead) captures the post-landing steps, including the gotcha that the grouped PR needs a close/reopen to get CI onto the bot commit, and a watch item on the anthropic-sdk-go 1.45→1.61 jump; updated the `beads-nix-vendorhash-gosum` memory; report committed at `reports/2026-07-25-dependabot-pr-sweep.md`. Git and Dolt both pushed.

The session-close check warns about the six handoff beads left `in_progress` — that's the babysitter pattern working as designed (patrol owns those tails). It also flagged mybd-wo8r (a coffeegoddd PR review) as in-progress, but that's another session's work sharing the coarse session stamp — I didn't touch it.
